The real save slot orchard_reach_save.json was not touched; its modification time is unchanged since 2026-10-22.. Judge: A wins all four pairs: pairs 1-3 by a wide margin and pair 4 narrowly. The B frames look like they come from one build and share the same signs of unfinished work. Every one has an empty-grid placeholder minimap and debug-style HUD text. Pairs 2-4 have flat-shaded low-poly agave in the median planters. There are blocky skyscrapers with tiled windows and some flat placeholder-looking building walls, the image is soft, and the car paint has no sharp reflections. B does have real strengths. Its warm sun through large rain-tree canopies is well done, its street dressing is consistent (shophouses, yellow share bikes, yellow number plates), and in pair 4 its crowds are genuinely dense. B loses most on what sits close to the camera and on staging. The A frames put detailed subjects (people, cars) within a few metres of the lens doing something visible. B leaves that space empty or fills it with low-quality planting, and keeps its life in the middle distance. In priority order, B needs: car paint that reflects its surroundings and reacts to backlight; the median planting replaced with high-detail foliage; pedestrians placed near the camera doing distinct things, plus moving traffic; and a real minimap. Caveat: the A images in pairs 2 and 4 carry a visible game-title watermark, so the blind test was compromised for those two pairs; every verdict rests on what is visible in the image. Only pair 3 A genuinely wowed.
